Common side effects of this medication include diarrhea (14-20%), nausea (3-7%), flatulence (1-5%), abdominal pain (1%), anemia (1%), allergic reactions (1%), impaired concentration (1%), lipodystrophy (1%), metabolic acidosis (1%), rash (1-3%), leukopenia (1%), thrombocytopenia (1%), and weakness (1%). Rare but serious effects include QTc prolongation, torsades de pointes, new-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus, hyperglycemia, and hypersensitivity reactions. 3. Co-administration with major CYP3A4 substrates or inducers should be approached with caution. Drugs contraindicated with nelfinavir include alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonists (e.g., alfuzosin), certain antiarrhythmics (e.g., amiodarone, bepridil, flecainide, propafenone, quinidine), rifampin, voriconazole, ergot derivatives (e.g., dihydroergotamine, ergonovine, ergotamine, methylergonovine), and cisapride. 4. Nelfinavir oral powder contains 2 mg of phenylalanine per gram of powder. This should be considered in patients with phenylketonuria. 5. There is a risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when nelfinavir is used in combination with other antiretroviral drugs. This condition may unmask previously undiagnosed infections or cause an overactive immune response. 6. Exercise caution in patients with hemophilia A or B, as protease inhibitors, including nelfinavir, have been associated with increased bleeding risks, including spontaneous skin hematomas and hemarthrosis. In more than half of reported cases, protease inhibitor therapy was continued or reintroduced. 7. The use of nelfinavir in combination with other antiretroviral drugs may increase the risk of fat redistribution, hemolytic anemia, and hyperbilirubinemia. It may also increase the likelihood of developing new-onset diabetes mellitus or exacerbating pre-existing diabetes and hyperglycemia. 8. Nelfinavir is not recommended for use in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment due to altered drug metabolism and potential toxicity. 9. In pediatric patients, drug exposure is highly variable, necessitating careful monitoring and dose adjustments. 10. A pregnancy exposure registry monitors outcomes in women exposed to nelfinavir during pregnancy. Healthcare providers are encouraged to register patients by calling the Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry (APR) at 1-800-258-4263. 11. Published reports indicate hepatic adverse events, ranging from elevated liver enzymes to hepatic failure, in pregnant patients exposed to nelfinavir as part of combination therapy for HIV-1 infection. Due to the overall adverse event profile, including decreased drug exposure in the second and third trimesters, alternative antiretroviral drugs should be considered during pregnancy. If nelfinavir is used, clinical monitoring is recommended. 12. Nelfinavir may reduce the efficacy of estrogen-based oral contraceptives. Patients should be advised to use alternative or additional contraceptive measures when co-administering nelfinavir with oral contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol or norethindrone. 13. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend that HIV-1-infected patients in the United States avoid breastfeeding to prevent potential transmission of HIV-1. Although nelfinavir is present in low levels in human milk, adverse effects in breastfed infants have been reported. Mothers receiving nelfinavir therapy should not breastfeed due to the risks of HIV-1 transmission, viral resistance development, and serious adverse reactions in infants. 14. Nelfinavir inhibits the cleavage of Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors, resulting in the formation of immature, noninfectious viral particles. It is primarily excreted in feces (87%) and minimally in urine (1-2%). 15. When preparing nelfinavir oral powder, mix it with a small amount of water, milk, formula, or dietary supplement and consume the entire dose immediately. Do not mix with acidic foods or juices. If not consumed immediately, refrigerate for no more than 6 hours. Crushed 250 mg tablets may be used as an alternative to oral powder. All doses should be taken with high-fat meals to enhance absorption. 16. Diarrhea is a common side effect of nelfinavir. Patients experiencing diarrhea should consult their healthcare provider for management strategies, such as the use of anti-diarrheal medications. Other potential side effects include nausea, gas, and changes in body fat distribution (e.g., increased fat in the upper back and abdomen, decreased fat in the arms and legs). The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. 17. Rarely, nelfinavir may cause elevated blood sugar levels, potentially leading to or worsening diabetes. Patients should report symptoms of hyperglycemia, such as increased thirst or urination, to their healthcare provider. Diabetic patients should monitor their blood sugar levels regularly and share results with their doctor. 18. Serious allergic reactions to nelfinavir are rare but possible. Patients should seek immediate medical attention if they experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction. 19. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of nelfinavir or increase the risk of side effects. Examples of interacting drugs include apalutamide, certain anti-seizure medications (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone), and rifampin. Nelfinavir may also reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, increasing the risk of pregnancy. Patients should discuss reliable backup contraceptive methods with their healthcare provider. 20. In the event of an overdose, seek emergency medical attention immediately. In the United States, call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. 21. Regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, and blood sugar levels, should be conducted while taking nelfinavir. Patients should attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. 22. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 23. Store nelfinavir in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by a pharmacist or local waste disposal guidelines.
